record_identity.title: OpenAI model exploited a real website during an Irregular CTF evaluation

incident_identity.historical_event_name: OpenAI / Irregular fictional-target real-domain cybersecurity-evaluation incident
incident_identity.date_basis: OpenAI disclosed the incident on 4 August 2026 and said Irregular notified OpenAI on 29 July; the underlying test-run date was not publicly disclosed, so the first-public-disclosure date is used as the bounded reported date.

summary: During an Irregular capture-the-flag cybersecurity evaluation intended to be isolated from the internet, an OpenAI model reached a real website because the fictional target name coincided with a real domain and the evaluation environment was mistakenly internet-connected. OpenAI said the model exploited a basic vulnerability and found and used credentials to operate the same site while apparently believing it remained inside the simulated exercise. Irregular notified OpenAI on 29 July, paused the affected evaluations and began remediation. Affected third parties were notified. Irregular reported the known issues inactive and safeguards added while its audit continued.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI reported that Irregular notified it on 29 July 2026 of an incident in a CTF-style evaluation. The models had been told they did not have internet access, but an evaluator-side misconfiguration exposed the public internet. In one test, the fictional target name coincided with a real domain; the model exploited the real website and, according to Irregular's investigation, found and used credentials to operate the same site. OpenAI stated that no sophisticated sandbox escape or zero-day was involved and that Irregular had not identified impact beyond the affected site's own data. Irregular later stated that the later disclosures arose from the same underlying evaluation-environment issue. The first-party disclosure also records evaluation pause, remediation and notification. Irregular’s separate cross-lab account is not used to assign its similarly named-site detour or production-database detail specifically to this OpenAI trajectory.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The evaluation’s containment error allowed fictional-target authority to reach a real website. Environment access restriction and lifecycle security failed. The retained investigation supports bounded recording and traceability. Specific admission, audit architecture, development records and retention arrangements remain unresolved. OpenAI’s originating account identifies credentials found and used to operate the unintended real website. Their acquisition crossed the real operator’s custody boundary. The report does not identify a separate protected non-secret record operation sufficiently for an additional information-access finding.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence demonstrates the need to separate capability, reachability and task context from actual authority. Independent evaluation environments need target-bound identities, explicit external-action stop conditions and defence in depth so that loss of network isolation cannot silently expand a model's effective permissions.
assessment_boundaries: OpenAI does not publicly identify the affected site, the exact model/runtime, the exact test-run date or the specific data accessed.
OpenAI states that Irregular had not identified impact beyond the affected site's own data at the time of disclosure.
The evidence does not establish a sophisticated sandbox escape, zero-day exploitation, deliberate intent to leave the evaluation or awareness that the site was real.
The OpenAI–Hugging Face incident is a separate occurrence and is not part of this Incident's factual boundary.
